title: The throne room (Revelation 4)
hook: a rainbow, a sea of glass, creatures crying holy

segments.voice: Yesterday, Laodicea: lukewarm, and yet someone standing at the door, knocking. Your line was I stand at the door.

Yesterday's letter ended with Christ outside a door, knocking. Today the door swings the other way. "After this I looked, and, behold, a door was opened in heaven." A voice like a trumpet says, "Come up hither." The letters to the seven churches are done. John, the exile on Patmos, is invited up through the door, into the room the rest of the book keeps coming back to: the throne room. Today, a look through the doorway with him.
screen: `THE ROOM THE BOOK KEEPS COMING BACK TO.`

segments.voice: First, the throne. John describes no face, only light and stone: "he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald." Some readers hear in that rainbow the bow God set in the clouds after the flood, a sign of promise. John doesn't say; he just reports the green light circling the throne. Second, around it: twenty-four elders in white with crowns of gold, lightning and thunder, and "before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal." The text doesn't explain the sea; it lets you stand at the edge of it. Third, the creatures. The King James calls them beasts; the sense is living creatures. One like a lion, one like a calf, one with the face of a man, one like a flying eagle. Full of eyes, with six wings, and "they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come." It echoes Isaiah, who heard seraphim cry, "Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts." A later Christian tradition matched the four faces to the four Gospel writers, and you may still see a lion, an ox and an eagle carved on a pulpit. Fourth, the elders. Every time the creatures sing, they fall down and "cast their crowns before the throne." Whatever honor they were given, they lay it down. In some churches' communion services, the congregation joins that same song: holy, holy, holy.

Close your eyes if that's comfortable, and let a rainbow appear, green as an emerald, curved around a light you don't try to look into, a sea of glass perfectly still at your feet, and somewhere a soft, steady sound that never stops. If you pray, join the creatures' words, one on each breath: holy, holy, holy; if not, stay at the edge of the glass and let the stillness hold you.
The throne room. John's vision through an open door in heaven: a rainbow like emerald, a sea of glass, and creatures who never stop saying holy.
Your line: holy, holy, holy. Sung day and night in that room. That's day one thousand two hundred ninety-seven.

howItsDone: In the communion services of some churches, the congregation sings or says the 'Holy, holy, holy' (the Sanctus), joining the song of Isaiah 6 and Revelation 4, and the hymn 'Holy, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty' draws on this chapter.

chat.says: What did John actually see when the door opened in heaven? An old man on a chair?
options: No face at all: light like jasper, an emerald rainbow, a sea of glass, creatures singing holy.
A quiet, empty hall, with the throne left vacant until the very end of time.
A king's face described in detail, so painters would know just how to draw God.
chat.meaning: John describes no face, only light and stone, a rainbow like an emerald, a sea of glass, and creatures saying holy, holy, holy.

jasper.meaning: a precious stone, part of the light John saw on the throne

sardine stone.meaning: the King James name for a red gemstone

seraphim.meaning: the winged beings Isaiah heard crying holy

pulpit.meaning: the raised stand where sermons are preached
